## The data the models fit on

Each model fits on one row per calendar month. The table gives the last 12 rows, so a reader
can see the shape and the units of the inputs. Section 2 gives the source and the release
date of each column.

Snow water equivalent is the depth of water held in the snowpack. A water year runs from
October 1 to September 30. `kaf` is thousand acre-feet, a volume of water.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
inputs = FileAttachment("data/latest.json").json().then(d => d.inputs ?? {columns: [], rows: []})
labels = ({
  month: "Month",
  avg_elevation: "Elevation (ft)",
  swe_eom_gsl: "Snow water equivalent (in)",
  prec_wy_eom_gsl: "Water-year precipitation (in)",
  head_diff_ft: "South arm minus north arm (ft)",
  inflow_kaf_total: "River inflow (kaf)"
})
inputTable = inputs.rows.length ? Inputs.table(inputs.rows, {
  columns: inputs.columns,
  header: Object.fromEntries(inputs.columns.map(c => [c, labels[c] ?? c])),
  format: Object.fromEntries(inputs.columns.filter(c => c !== "month").map(c => [c, v => Number.isFinite(v) ? v.toFixed(2) : "—"])),
  rows: 12
}) : html`<p class="empty-state compact">The sample appears with the first complete issue.</p>`
```

## Public record

The project keeps every forecast it has issued. A forecast is never changed after the date
on it, so a reader can compare it against the gauge later.

Each forecast stores its numbers, its interval, the weights the model fitted, the range of
dates it was fitted on, the state of the data on the issue date, and the contribution of
each input.

- [Dated forecasts](https://github.com/jcblsn/gsl-forecast/tree/main/forecasts)
- [Model source](https://github.com/jcblsn/gsl-forecast/tree/main/src/forecasting)
- [USGS gauge 10010000](https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/10010000/)
